p.PACKAGE-INSTALLS-A-CONFLICT-RESOLUTION-D: A `flow` package that installs a conflict-resolution discipline for projects where two writers — a human and a coding agent — edit one file set.

p.CONTRADICTIONS-ARE-NORMAL-COOPERATION-NO: The two *will* write contradictory things; that is normal cooperation, not an error.

p.WHAT-THE-DISCIPLINE-FORBIDS-IS-RESOLVING: What the discipline forbids is resolving a contradiction silently: priorities are fixed in advance, disagreement travels through visible REVIEW markers, and the case where the spec is simply silent gets a conservative-default ladder instead of invented semantics.

p.the-core-law-fits-on-one-line: The core law fits on one line:

p.HUMAN-CHANGES-THE-SPEC-CODE-CONFORMS-AND: The human may change the spec; code must conform to the spec; tests are the spec in executable form; volatile state files are records, dead last.

p.package-contents-lead: This package ships three pieces of content plus a boot snippet:

item.CONTENT-THE-PROTOCOL: `spec/flows/conflict-protocol/CONFLICT-PROTOCOL.md` — the full protocol: why conflicts are normal, the hierarchy and what each relation means operationally, the four-step REVIEW-marker protocol, the marker lifecycle, and a worked example of what one silent change costs (one bug becoming three, plus two weeks of git archaeology).

item.CONTENT-THE-UNCERTAINTY-PROTOCOL: `spec/flows/conflict-protocol/uncertainty-protocol.md` — the spec-is-silent path: re-read the spec, re-read the reference, check the closest analog, then conservative default + REVIEW + report; what "conservative" means (cheapest to reverse), and when to stop and ask instead.

item.CONTENT-THE-FAILURE-MODES: `spec/flows/conflict-protocol/failure-modes.md` — three named failures with recovery drills: the silent spec edit, the stale state file after a crash, and the self-contradicting spec.

item.CONTENT-THE-BOOT-SNIPPET: `spec/boot/35-flow-conflict-protocol.md` — boot snippet loaded at session start: the hierarchy one-liner, the REVIEW contract, the uncertainty ladder, and the never-do list.

p.UNINSTALL-REMOVES-EVERY-FILE-THE-PACKAGE: Uninstalling removes every file the package wrote, including the boot snippet.

item.COMPOSES-TWO-PROCESS-MODEL: `flow:two-process-model` — the hierarchy is that model's law #1; this package is its enforcement arm.

item.COMPOSES-WAL: `flow:wal` — the WAL sits at the hierarchy's tail as a volatile record; the stale-WAL recovery drill lives in this package's failure-modes document.

item.COMPOSES-ADDRESSABLE-SPECS: `flow:addressable-specs` — a REVIEW marker and a correction both cite the violated anchor; addressability is what makes a dispute cost twenty tokens instead of two hundred.

item.COMPOSES-DECISION-RECORDS: `flow:decision-records` — a resolved conflict often ends as a recorded decision, so the same question is not re-litigated next quarter.

p.practice-extracted-from-the-book: The practice is extracted from *AI-native development*, chapters 1–2: the priority hierarchy and the memory-fence framing come from chapter 1 (two co-processors sharing files as their only IPC); the REVIEW protocol, the silent-change data race, and the three failure modes come from chapter 2.

p.CHAPTERS-SHIP-IN-RUSSIAN-INSIDE-REDBOOK: Both chapters ship in Russian inside `flow:redbook` at `spec/book/ru/`.
